Omalo and Tusheti

Georgia's most isolated mountain region, beyond the Abano Pass — 4x4 only, and only from June to October.

Time needed
8 h
From Tbilisi
220 km · 6:30
Road
4x4 only
Car needed
Off-road 4x4
Season
June–September
Entry
free

Tusheti lies north of the main ridge of the Caucasus, and the only way in is over the Abano Pass at 2,850 metres: seventy kilometres of gravel from Pshaveli to Omalo, narrow the whole way, cut into the slope, with no barriers. The road appears regularly on lists of the world's most dangerous drives, and it earns the reputation honestly. This is the single hardest constraint of any trip in Georgia and it dictates everything else about the visit.

Omalo is the regional centre. Lower Omalo is the village with guesthouses and a shop; Upper Omalo sits on the hill above it around a cluster of Tushetian defensive towers that has become the visual signature of the region. Trails run out from here to Diklo, Shenako, Dartlo and Chesho, villages a few hours apart on foot that form the classic multi-day trekking circuit.

The road normally opens in early June and closes at the end of October. In winter Tusheti empties almost completely — a few dozen people stay, reachable only by helicopter. The summer window is therefore short, and weather on the pass can turn within a couple of hours. Mobile coverage and internet are patchy, and there is no ATM anywhere in the region.

Practical advice

This is not an ordinary day out. You need a genuine high-clearance 4x4 and a driver comfortable with exposed gravel, and you must confirm in advance whether your rental agreement permits the Abano Pass — many companies explicitly exclude it; see our /terms/. Plan at least two nights, since a day trip makes no sense. Carry cash, spare fuel, warm layers and your own medication: even the pharmacy in Omalo is minimal, and the nearest hospital is hours away.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi to Akhmeta and on to Pshaveli the road is asphalt — about 150 km covered in two and a half hours. At Pshaveli the real section begins: seventy kilometres of gravel over the Abano Pass, which realistically takes four hours or more. That gives 220 km and around six and a half hours in total without stops. The last fuel station is in Akhmeta; there is none between there and Omalo, so start with a full tank. After rain the surface deteriorates sharply and landslides are common.

Nearby places

Monastery

Alaverdi Cathedral

An eleventh-century cathedral rising fifty metres out of the Alazani plain — for centuries the tallest building in Georgia.

Fortress

Gremi

The citadel of Kakheti's lost capital — a 1565 church and tower on a hill above the Alazani Valley.

Monastery

Nekresi Monastery

One of the oldest surviving churches in Georgia, on a wooded slope with a sweeping view over the Alazani Valley.
